objective: Prove, in the style of Ben-Sasson and Wigderson's size-width argument, that a parity decision tree of size s for a CNF's false-clause search gives an F2 polynomial-calculus refutation of degree at most log2 s + w; so a size lower bound for tree-like Res(xor) on the count follows from an F2 polynomial-calculus degree lower bound (backlog B84).
status: Proved 2026-11-10: a parity decision tree with s leaves gives an F2 polynomial-calculus refutation of degree log2 s + w (Ben-Sasson-Wigderson's induction with linear queries), so tree-like Res(xor) on the sphere's count has size at least 2^(deg_PC - 3): the size question is the F2 polynomial-calculus degree (B84).
title: Tree-like Res(xor) size is bounded by F2 polynomial-calculus degree
